entries.text: The sage does not hoard. The more he gives to others, the more he has for himself.
At the center of your being you have the answer; you know who you are and you know what you want.
Nature does not hurry, yet everything is accomplished.
A journey of a thousand miles begins beneath one's feet.
When I let go of what I am, I become what I might be.
The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
Knowing others is intelligence; knowing yourself is true wisdom. Mastering others is strength; mastering yourself is true power.
Silence is a source of great strength.
Be content with what you have; rejoice in the way things are. When you realize there is nothing lacking, the whole world belongs to you.
Water is fluid, soft, and yielding. But water will wear away rock, which is rigid and cannot yield.
The softest things in the world overcome the hardest.
To the mind that is still, the whole universe surrenders.
Empty yourself of everything. Let the mind rest at peace.
When the student is ready, the teacher will appear.
The flame that burns twice as bright burns half as long.
Do the difficult things while they are easy and do the great things while they are small.
A good traveler has no fixed plans and is not intent on arriving.
He who knows others is wise; he who knows himself is enlightened.
The sage wears coarse clothing, but carries jade within.
Care about what other people think and you will always be their prisoner.
Govern a great nation as you would cook a small fish: do not overdo it.
Act without doing; work without effort.
When nothing is done, nothing is left undone.
Those who know do not speak. Those who speak do not know.
Be really whole and all things will come to you.
If you realize that all things change, there is nothing you will try to hold on to.
The farther one travels, the less one knows.
Life is a series of natural and spontaneous changes. Do not resist them — that only creates sorrow.
Simplicity, patience, compassion. These three are your greatest treasures.
Mastering others is strength. Mastering yourself is true power.
New beginnings are often disguised as painful endings.
The wise find pleasure in water; the virtuous find pleasure in hills.
The highest good is like water. Water benefits all things and does not compete.
To know yet to think that one does not know is best.
Stop thinking, and end your problems.
The sage does not attempt anything very big, and thus achieves greatness.
Because she believes in herself, she doesn't try to convince others. Because she is content with herself, she doesn't need others' approval.
Do your work, then step back. The only path to serenity.
She who stands on tiptoe doesn't stand firmly. She who rushes ahead doesn't go far.
Great acts are made up of small deeds.
Respond intelligently even to unintelligent treatment.
Fill your bowl to the brim and it will spill. Keep sharpening your knife and it will blunt.
When goodness is lost, there is morality. When morality is lost, there is ritual.
Being deeply loved by someone gives you strength, while loving someone deeply gives you courage.
The sage has no mind of her own. She makes the minds of others her mind.
